pages.insight: The deck contrasts iid supervised samples with dependent RL trajectories and frames both domains as learning mappings from inputs or states to outputs or actions.
The policy-optimization slide shows a state-to-action policy network, sampled actions, discounted rewards, and a REINFORCE-style policy update; it contains no critic or shared actor-critic trunk.

agentReview.summary: Independent review identified the split from shared state features into actor and critic objectives as the hardest prose-only model. The final design makes the fixed advantage signal and separate parameter updates explicit without implying that shared trunk parameters receive only one loss.

implementation.accessibility: One state enters shared features and then actor and critic heads. The policy loss uses log action probability and advantage y minus V. A stop mark on the V-to-advantage path blocks policy-loss gradients into the critic. The value loss is an illustrative squared error against fixed target y. Separate dashed paths return each loss through its own head into the shared features. Solid lines construct the losses; dashed lines indicate parameter-gradient ownership. All labels use at least 12 viewBox units in a 360-unit-wide composition. Meaning is also encoded by positions, words, line styles, and numbers, not color alone.
